### Borea v0.6.0-dev.2: test build for developers

This pre-release is for the Borea team and developers who want to test v0.6.0 before it is released.
It is not for users.
For normal use, stay on v0.5.2.
It builds on v0.6.0-dev.1.
The list below covers only what changed since that build.
Tell us what did not work: [Discord](https://discord.gg/nt4fK4QuTz) | [GitHub issues](https://github.com/KSAModding/Borea/issues)

#### Please test these first

- Share a vehicle, with two people.
  On the Vehicles tab of Discover, use "Share your vehicle", or use the Share button on a vehicle row of your instance.
  Choose the vehicle, check the proposed mods, describe it, check it with the share host, and publish.
  The last step gives you the link.
  The second person finds the vehicle in Discover and installs it.
  A publish goes to the real index, so share only an item that is meant to be listed.
- A new version of a shared vehicle.
  Share a vehicle that you shared before, and check that Borea names the listing and asks if this is a new version before it asks for any field.
- Share a save.
  Do the same steps for a save.
  Check that the save has no automatic cover, and that it loads in the game after the second person installed it.
- Pictures and the automatic cover.
  On the Describe step, add up to 6 pictures.
  On the Publish step of a new vehicle, check the cover picture that Borea draws, and also use your own picture or leave the cover out.
  After the publish, the Done step shows each picture with its progress.
  Stop your network once, and check that a failed picture never undoes the publish and that "Try again" sends only what is missing.
- Thumbnails in Discover.
  Open the Vehicles tab and scroll.
  Rows without an icon get a picture that Borea draws on your computer.
  Do this once with a slow network, and once with a vehicle that needs a mod that you did not install.
  The picture must then show boxes and the note "Mods missing", and it must be drawn again after you install the mod.
  Turn off "Load images from author hosts" in Settings, General, and check that Discover then fetches nothing.
- An install link.
  Open a `borea://install` link of a vehicle or save.
  Borea must plan it with its mods and wait for one click.
  Test a link with a version, a vehicle that is already in the instance, and a name that is already taken.
- Update hints.
  Share or install a vehicle, then publish a new version of it.
  The Home count and "Update all" on the instance page must include vehicles and saves, and the row must show "Update to X" with a progress bar.
- Change a listing and take a version down.
  Open the page of a listing that you shared.
  In the "You shared this" block, change the text of the page, then take down a version.
  Read the warning of the take-down before you click.
  Use a listing that you can lose.
- Update all with many mods.
  Install many mods, with an older kept build too if you can, and press "Update all".
  Check that the window lists every mod with both versions, that the plan does not stop with a limit message, and that Stop works while it runs.
- The conflict window.
  Add a mod that conflicts with an installed mod.
  A window must name both mods and say which one declares the conflict.
  When Borea installed the other mod and nothing needs it, test "Remove X and continue".
- Going back: after you tested, read "Before you go back to v0.5.2" below, and then start v0.5.2 again.

#### Before you go back to v0.5.2

- v0.5.2 does not know kept builds.
  When it saves an instance, it drops the kept build of that instance, and the instance then starts on the current build.
  The copy itself stays on the disk and still uses space.
- v0.5.2 does not know the records of the vehicles and saves that Borea installed.
  The vehicles and saves stay in the instance, but v0.5.2 does not update or remove them as installed content.
- This build writes a new file, `shared-content.toml`, into the Borea folder (`%LocalAppData%\Borea` on Windows).
  It holds the vehicles and saves that you shared, with the host, the listing and the folder, and your last author and license. v0.5.2 does not read or change this file.
  If you rename a shared vehicle or save in v0.5.2, the entry keeps the old folder name, and this build then does not show the item as shared.
  Delete the file if you want Borea to forget what you shared.
  A listing on the host stays online.
- Borea writes the game folder of the instance into `StarMapConfig.json` before each start, and writes your normal game folder back when a game on a kept build ends.
  If you closed Borea or used `borea launch` while such a game ran, set `GameLocation` in `StarMapConfig.json` back to your game folder by hand, or start the instance once more from this version.
- A kept build is a full copy of KSA, about 2.8 GB on Windows.

#### New since v0.6.0-dev.1

Sharing a vehicle or save
- Sharing has its own steps: choose, describe, check with the host, publish, done.
  Nothing goes to a host until every required field is valid, and the page says under the Next button what is still missing.
- The first step lists every vehicle or save of all your instances.
  The active instance comes first, then the others by last played.
  A vehicle that is an unchanged copy of someone else's vehicle cannot go out under a new name.
- The share starts from visible places: a Share button on the row of your own vehicle or save, a block in the filter panel of the Vehicles and Saves tabs, and the start of the listing page.
- The describe step asks for a name, your name, one sentence and a license from a plain list.
  The short name, the description and the tags are under "More options".
  "Edit all fields" opens the full form with what you typed.
- The mods of the item show in plain words.
  Players who add the item get these mods too, and a row says when a mod is not in Discover, so players cannot install it.
- Borea finds the listing of a new version by its local record, its install record or its install folder, and then by its id.
  It asks before any field if this is a new version.
- The publish step opens the sign-in page of the host with the code filled in, shows the limit and the rules of the host, and shows one line when all checks passed.
  A failed check comes first, with the message of the host and a rename when the name is the problem.
- Every known error of a share host has a plain text in your language and a next step.
  A refused token signs in again by itself and keeps your sign-in.
  A busy host no longer loses it.
- The done step says that everyone can download the item now, gives Open page and Copy link, and says when the item shows in Discover.
  The link goes to the page of the item on the Borea site, and Open page opens the page of the host.
- "Save a zip file instead" is for players who only want a file or have no share host.
  It says that nothing is published.
- Borea remembers on your computer what you shared.
  The row says "Shared on {host}", and the next share starts with your last author and license.
- Pictures: up to 6 PNG, JPEG or WebP pictures of at most 10 MB each go up one at a time after the publish, and the first is the cover.
  A listing that has a cover keeps it.
  A host that offers no pictures gets none.
- Automatic cover: on a new vehicle listing, the Publish step shows a picture that Borea draws from the vehicle and says that it becomes public as the cover.
  Only the PNG goes up, and no game file.
  You can use your own picture or leave it out.
  A vehicle with a part that Borea cannot find gets no cover.
- You can change the text of a listing that you shared, or take down one of its versions, from the page of the item or from the done step.
  A take-down names the version and says that it cannot be undone.
  A host that does not offer these requests gets a line that says so.
- A game that runs stops a share with a banner before you type anything.
  Borea also stops writing the share files while a game that Borea did not start runs.

Vehicles and saves in the app
- The page of a vehicle shows its parts, stages and needed mods as facts.
  The 3D preview has "Save picture" and "Expand view", and the expanded view fills the window with the same camera.
- Fuel lines show in the 3D preview, on the route that the game gives them.
  A hose uses its texture when your files have it.
  A fuel line that cannot be drawn is left out, and the preview still opens.
- Discover draws a small picture on your computer for each vehicle row that has no icon.
  Borea downloads the vehicle file once per version, up to 5 MB, from a share host that keeps no download count.
  All other hosts keep the normal icon.
- About the 3D preview fetch: when a vehicle file is not on your computer, Borea can download it by itself for the picture or the preview, and the host then sees your IP address.
  "Load images from author hosts" in Settings, General, switches this off, and then every vehicle file waits for a click.
  The privacy page names it.
- After you install a vehicle or save, the row and the page show numbered steps with the real menu names of the game and a Play button.
  "Open instance" goes to the new row and marks it.
- The Vehicles and Saves tabs of Discover always open, and an empty tab says how to be the first to share.
  A vehicle or save without a picture shows an icon.
- The update of a vehicle or save is a link on its row, with a progress bar.
  The Home count and "Update all" include vehicles and saves.
  A vehicle or save that asks a question waits on its row and is not overwritten.
- Home shows four groups: recently updated mods, new mods, new vehicles and the most downloaded mods.
  Each group links to the Discover tab and sort that show the same order.
- `borea://install` links work for vehicles and saves, with a version in the link.
  The Borea site has a page for every vehicle and save, with the host named as the source.
- A name with German letters or accents gives a readable proposed id.

Updates and conflicts
- "Update all" opens a window.
  It lists every mod that changes with both versions, a link to the changelog of each mod, and a warning when a save can lose vehicles.
  The button says what it does, for example "Update 3 mods (12.6 MB)".
  A required choice comes first.
- The plan search no longer stops with a few mods.
  Borea tries mods together only when they require, recommend or conflict with each other, so mods with no relation no longer multiply.
  With 31 mods the plan was ready in about a millisecond where it stopped at the limit before.
  An older kept build now shows which mods do not fit it.
- If a plan still stops at the limit, the message names the mods and tells you to change fewer of them at once.
  The window stays alive during a plan, and Stop on the row and Ctrl+C in the CLI end it.
- A plan that stops on a conflict opens a window that names both mods, which one declares the conflict, and why nothing changed.
  It offers "Remove X and continue" when Borea installed the other mod and nothing needs it.
  Installs, updates, modlist imports, modpacks and manual replacements show the same window.
- A mod that conflicts with an installed mod now names the conflict.
  Before, it read as a missing release.

For stewards and pack authors
- The Steward page has a Statistics tab.
  It counts the index that Borea already holds, and it sends no request.
  It shows the listings in total, the mods that are not blocked on the current build, the listings with upkeep problems, and the downloads in total, with tables for dependencies and upkeep.
- The privacy page says what sharing sends to a share host and what becomes public.
  It names the requests that run without a click, and it corrects the switch of the KSA master server check.

Everything else
- The Simplified Chinese texts of the new steps are in English for now. 303 texts are not translated yet: the share steps, the Update all window, the conflict window and the Statistics tab.
  Four older texts still show the Chinese of their older English wording.
- The new texts are in German.
- Changelogs show in compact Markdown.
- Many tests are more reliable on slow computers, and the code has clearer comments and less duplication.

#### How to get the next test builds

With the default update channel, "Stable releases", Borea does not tell you about pre-releases like this one.
To see them, open Settings, General, and set "Update channel for Borea" to "All releases, dev builds included".
"Check for updates at start" must be on.
When v0.6.0 is released, every channel tells you about it.
